MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  February 15, 2010

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor MacLean at
6:04 p.m., on February 15, 2010 at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on February 10, 2010, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

ROLL CALL

Present:  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Schlicht
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor MacLean

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

INVOCATION: Council Member Ury

PUBLIC COMMENTS

City Council Minutes  1  February 15, 2010
 Joyce Saltzgiver, M.V.: read from an email written by resident Joe Holtzman in which he
questioned Dale Tyler’s motives and stated that the Right to Vote Initiative is flawed. She also
expressed her objection to the new cut-through on the median strip on Casta del Sol Drive.

Valerie Maginnis, M.V.: thanked Mayor MacLean for his unswerving support of the City’s
library.

Sherry M. Butterfield, M.V.: thanked Mayor MacLean for his dedicated service to the
community and she welcomed Council Member-elect Dave Leckness.

Hugh Armstrong, M.V.: stated that the recall was a waste of money and time and brought
unneeded divisiveness to the City. He thanked Mayor MacLean for his service and
congratulated Dave Leckness.

Anna T. Boyce, M.V.: thanked Mayor MacLean for his years of dedication, support and
wonderful improvements to our City. She announced that the City provided over 600 H1N1
vaccines and 400 flu vaccines at the recent flu shot clinic and she thanked staff for supporting
these clinics and the five nurses who volunteer their time.

Sharon Cody, M.V.: thanked Mayor MacLean for his nearly eight years of service to our City.
She stated that the City has never been more beautiful and it is in a great state of financial health.
She also welcomed Council Member-elect Dave Leckness.

David Allen, M.V.: thanked the voters who understood the issues with the recall and he
reminded those who did not vote to remember that their vote does count, especially in local
elections. He thanked Dave Leckness for stepping up to run for City Council and giving the
voters an alternate candidate.

Helen Workun, M.V.: congratulated Dave Leckness for stepping up to the plate and she stated
that this election is a bittersweet victory. It is sweet because our City has been temporarily saved
from a small group of activists but the recall of Lance MacLean should have never happened.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, Schlicht and Ury
NOES:  MacLean
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

City Council Minutes  2  February 15, 2010
   Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of February 1, 2010, as
  presented.

2.  Official Results of the February 2, 2010, Special Municipal Election

  (1) Adopted Resolution 10-05 Reciting the Fact That a Special Municipal Election Was
  Held on February 2, 2010, and Declaring the Result and Such Other Matters.

Mayor MacLean stated that his no vote is a reflection of the results of the election. It has nothing
to do with Neal Kelley and the Registrar of Voters; he feels that they did a tremendous job with
the vote count. Mayor MacLean noted that his no vote is a personal protest because the election
should have never happened in the first place knowing some of the irregularities that took place.

COUNCIL RELATED CEREMONIAL ITEMS

3.  Comments from Outgoing Mayor MacLean

  Mayor MacLean outlined the things that he and the Council have accomplished during
  his time serving the City as a Council Member. He thanked his family and his
  supporters, former Council Members, City staff, and the residents who gave him the
  honor and privilege of serving. Mayor MacLean extended his best wishes to all of the
  Council Members, including Dave Leckness, and stated that he hopes the Council will
  continue prioritizing the projects that he has worked on but will not be here to complete.

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley presented Mayor MacLean with a City tile in recognition of his
  years of service to the City of Mission Viejo.

4.  Administration of Oath of Office

  City Clerk Karen Hamman administered the Oath of Office and presented the Certificate
  of Election to Dave Leckness.

5.  Comments from Council Member Dave Leckness

  Council Member Leckness thanked his campaign manager, his supporters, and his family.
  He stated that the City has been wounded by this recall and it's a shame that it was
  successful. He thanked Lance MacLean for his service and stated that it is time to start
  fresh and everyone needs to be part of that. Council Member Leckness discussed his
  experience in the community and expressed his desire to make a positive contribution on
  the City Council.

ROLL CALL

City Council Minutes  3  February 15, 2010
 Present:  Council Member Leckness
  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Schlicht
  Council Member Ury

CITY COUNCIL REORGANIZATION

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to appoint
  Dave Leckness as Mayor Pro Tem for the remainder of 2010.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to
  appoint Trish Kelley as Mayor for the remainder of 2010.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht

RECESS

At the hour of 6:52 p.m., Mayor Kelley declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 7:10
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

CONSENT CALENDAR (CONTINUED)

Item 21 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

24.  Agreement for Professional Services for the Preparation of an Environmental
  Impact Report to Update the Land Use, Conservation / Open Space, and
  Circulation Elements of the City General Plan; and Preparation of an Air Quality /
  Greenhouse Gas Reduction Element / Climate Action Plan.

City Council Minutes  6  February 15, 2010
   Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Ury, to
  approve agreement with AECOM in an amount not to exceed $200,000 for professional
  services.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

25.  June 8, 2010, Special Municipal Election for the Vote on Private and Public
  Property Land Use Regulation Initiative Measure

  City Clerk Karen Hamman presented the staff report.

  City Attorney Bill Curley displayed a PowerPoint presentation with preliminary
  comments on the Attorney's Impartial Analysis.

  The following expressed opposition to the measure and to the election: Joyce Saltzgiver,
  M.V.; Sharon Cody, M.V.; and Wendy Bucknum, M.V.

  Kristine Thalman, CEO of the Orange County Chapter of the Building Industry
  Association (BIA): announced that the BIA has gone through extensive review and
  analysis of this initiative and believes that it will have virtually little or no impact on their
  industry or the development community at large. The BIA suggests placing the measure
  on the November 2010 ballot to achieve maximum participation by the voters.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to divide
  the question and vote on items 1 through 5, deferring item 6 until the next meeting.

  Amended motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member
  Ledesma, to (1) adopt Resolution 10-07 Calling for the Holding of a Special Municipal
  Election on Tuesday, June 8, 2010, for the Submission of a Proposed Ordinance; (2)
  adopt Resolution 10-08 Requesting The Board of Supervisors of The County of Orange
  to Consolidate a Special Municipal Election to be Held on June 8, 2010, With the
  Statewide Primary Election to be Held on the Date Pursuant To Section 10403 of the
  Elections Code; (3) adopt Resolution 10-09 Setting Priorities for Filing Written
  Arguments Regarding an Initiative Measure and Directing the City Attorney to Prepare
  an Impartial Analysis; (4) adopt Resolution 10-10 Providing for the Filing of Rebuttal
  Arguments for Initiative Measures Submitted At Municipal Elections; (5) adopt
  Resolution 10-11 Amending the Fiscal Year 2009-2010 Budget in the Amount of
  $147,516 to Pay for the June 8, 2010, Special Election for an Initiative Measure; and (6)

City Council Minutes  7  February 15, 2010
   authorize Council Member Ury to file a written argument against the ordinance as
  permitted by Elections Code Section 9282.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

City Council Minutes  8  February 15, 2010
 27.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

29.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

30.  SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

City Manager Wilberg announced that he had nothing to report.

Council Member Schlicht inquired about the process for appealing a decision of the Planning and
Transportation Commission.

City Manager Wilberg recommended that she contact the City Clerk to obtain the proper appeal
form.

City Attorney’s Report

City Attorney Bill Curley suggested that Council Member Schlicht contact Director Chuck
Wilson for assistance with the wording of her appeal so, as the appellant, she can still participate
in the discussion and voting.

He further announced that Mayor Pro Tem Leckness will be required to disclose his real property
business interest in the Community Development Agency project area. At the next meeting Mr.
Leckness will be asked to note his interests in writing and those will be formalized in the
Minutes in order to meet the legal disclosure requirements.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS

31.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

City Council Minutes  9  February 15, 2010
   The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the staff report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the
  public record.

Council Member Ledesma

Council Member Ledesma congratulated Mayor Pro Tem Leckness and stated that he looks
forward to a good year.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht reminded everyone that it was President’s Day and she hopes people
look beyond it being just another three day weekend. She congratulated our Olympic hopefuls as
so far, the United States has the highest number of medals. She also recognized the troops who
protect our way of life. Council Member Schlicht announced that she is pleased to have Dave
Leckness up on the dais and she thinks the recall was a win-win for the community. She offered
her advice to Mayor Pro Tem Leckness to make sure he does what is right and fair.

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury announced that one of the biggest things coming to the Council over the
next few months is the waste disposal contract. He invited consultant Joe Sloan to provide an
update for the Council.

Joe Sloan, Sloan Vazquez: discussed the RFP process for the City’s solid waste contract and
announced that the proposals are due in the City Clerk’s office on Friday, February 19, 2010, at
4:00 p.m. He outlined the process thereafter and stated that Sloan and Vazquez will present their
recommendation at the Council meeting of April 19, 2010, with the final contract approval
scheduled in the month of May.

Council Member Ury thanked Lance MacLean for his service to the community and he noted the
extraordinary work that Mr. MacLean accomplished on the San Joaquin Hills Transportation
Corridor Agency. He also congratulated Mayor Pro Tem Dave Leckness.

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness thanked the Council Members and staff for welcoming him. He stated
that he has enjoyed the last few months and he looks forward to serving the residents.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley announced that she has been serving on the Southern California Army Advisory
Council for the past few months and she is in charge of the Outreach Committee which will
provide assistance and support to those members of the Army in this region. She encouraged
residents to give her a call if they’d like to join the Army Advisory Council or help her with the

City Council Minutes  10  February 15, 2010
 outreach efforts. She also invited members of the community to come to the Relay for Life
kickoff event on Thursday, February 18, 2010, at 6:00 p.m. at Mission Viejo Lexus. The City’s
Relay for Life will be held this year on June 6 and 7 at Saddleback College and she is the team
captain of Kelley’s Heroes. She encouraged those who would like to learn more about the Relay
or show support for this event to come to the kickoff on Thursday. Mayor Kelley discussed a
newspaper article that caught her eye in the Orange County Register. The Register has
recognized the best elementary school campuses in Orange County and she was pleased to see a
number of Mission Viejo schools honored: in the gold medal category, Bathgate Elementary
School. A silver medal was awarded to De Portola Elementary, Castille Elementary and
Marguerite M. O’Neill Elementary. In the bronze category, Cordillera Elementary, Montevideo
Elementary, Philip J. Reilly Elementary and La Tierra. Mayor Kelley congratulated the parents,
students, principals and teachers from these standout schools and she stated that she is proud and
pleased that we live in a city that provides such fine educational opportunities for our kids.
Mayor Kelley concluded her comments by noting that these are not the circumstances that she
envisioned for becoming Mayor however, she is willing, pleased and able to lead the Council for
the remainder of the year. She stated that a lot of people have been hurt, friendships have been
destroyed and she looks forward to a time when the city can put the divisive recall election
behind it. Mayor Kelley stated her goal for the year is to build bridges and to continue to put the
best interests of the City first.

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference With Real Property Negotiator Pursuant to Government Code Section
  54956.8. Real Property Denoted as Parcel 2 of Tentative Tract Map No. 16877, with
  a Common Address of 25565 Los Alisos Boulevard, Mission Viejo, California and
  Generally Situated Easterly of the Intersection of Jeronimo Road and Los Alisos
  Boulevard in the City of Mission Viejo Owned by Target Corporation. CDA
  Negotiators: Dennis Wilberg, CDA Executive Director/City Manager; Irwin
  Bornstein, Assistant City Manager; Charles Wilson, Director of Community
  Development; James Williams, Economic Advisor; Celeste Brady, CDA Special
  Counsel; William Curley, III, City Attorney/CDA General Counsel. Developer’s
  Negotiators: Bob Garrison of Lennar Homes of California, Inc., as Prospective
  Buyer from Target Corporation, and Roger Grable of Manatt Phelps, Counsel to
  Lennar. Under negotiation: Real property interests for affordable housing, the price
  and terms of payment thereof for above-listed Property pursuant to Affordable
  Housing Agreement. Factors Affecting Price and Terms under Negotiation:
  Recorded covenants, Scope and schedule of development of Property and
  Affordable housing requirements. Factors affecting time of payment: Conditions to
  closing, Due diligence period and Schedule of Project Development of Affordable
  Housing.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 9:01 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 9:45 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

City Council Minutes  11  February 15, 2010
 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there was nothing to report from Closed Session.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:46 p.m., there being no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting in memory of Leona Kelley to Monday, March 1,
2010, at 5:00 p.m.
